- HIGH `[review-edge-display-gap]`: Step 4 ("Show each edge's note in create's interactive step review") assumes the operator already sees each proposed step's `depends_on` edges at review time, but `create.py`'s interactive review (`_ask_change_type`) never renders `depends_on` at all — it prints only step id, title, proposed `change_type`, and rationale. `depends_on` is only ever echoed after the fact, as a read-only confirmation once a split has already been applied.
  - Fix: broaden step 4's own stated scope to also render each proposed step's `depends_on` ids in the interactive review — the same place the note will be shown — since neither exists there today, not just the note by itself.

## Conceptual completeness — reported, not auto-applied

Coverage gaps in the plan's own ideas are reported for visibility in this bare-plan audit. Apply actions for this axis are withheld until a complete detail bundle exists, so these findings are informational for now.

- MEDIUM `[canonical-extraction-notes]`: `create --from-existing` populates a plan's `depends_on` graph through two different code paths — the Claude step-proposal round-trip that step 3 (`Ask create's step proposal for a per-edge note...`) targets, and the deterministic canonical-shape reader (`plan_tool/canonical.py`'s `extract_canonical_steps`, wired through `create.extract_steps_from_canonical`), which builds `Step` objects straight off a `Depends on: N, M` markdown line with no Claude call at all — the whole point of that path is to skip Claude. The Overview's mechanism ("the same prompt turn that proposes `depends_on`") cannot fire on this second path, so any plan lifted from a canonical-shape seed gets zero `depends_on_notes` by construction, and the plan never states whether that is the intended, permanent state or a gap step 3 should also close.
  - Fix: add a sentence (in Architecture or step 3) saying the deterministic canonical-shape lift is deliberately out of scope for note-asking — consistent with notes being optional everywhere — so a `detail`-stage reader isn't left guessing whether `canonical.py` needs Claude-call machinery bolted onto its zero-Claude design.
- MEDIUM `[never-graded-note-content]`: The Architecture's "trap" warning and the acceptance criterion "No pass in this codebase grades, scores, or checks a note's content" are both asserted only in plan prose — no step or Testing bullet adds a test that would fail if a later change wired `depends_on_notes` into a scoring or gating path. This is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md's own "Withdrawn: the per-`change_type` test-ordering contract" section records costing real audit cycles the last time a plausible-sounding note field got graded, and the repo's own Tests-section rule says a "deliberately not" claim is "a claim to pin, not a fact to trust."
  - Fix: add a Testing bullet (owned by step 1 or step 6) for a coarse regression check — e.g. every reference to `depends_on_notes` outside `schema.py` and `create.py`'s authoring path only reads or carries the field, never scores or gates on it — so the fence the Risks section describes is enforced, not just documented.
- MEDIUM `[bench-carry-scope]`: Step 2's title lists "bench" alongside split/merge/scope-out as a place that "rewrites `depends_on`," but `plan_tool/bench.py`'s only `depends_on`-touching code either zeroes the field out for an isolated one-step scoring fixture (`_detail_files_coherence_issue_count`) or only reads it to check a split's shape (`_proposal_split_satisfied`) — neither renumbers or carries an existing multi-edge graph the way the split/merge/scope-out primitives do. A `detail`-stage author could read step 2's title as asking for bench-side carry-through code with no real target, when the actual gap, if any, is in the `benchmarks/corpus/` fixture files' own `Depends on:`-style answer keys, not in `bench.py`'s logic.
  - Fix: reword step 2 to name the real bench surface (the corpus fixtures' answer keys) instead of "bench rewrite depends_on," or drop "bench" from the title if no corpus fixture needs updating.
- HIGH `[edge-rewrite-note-policy]`: Step 2 says split, merge, and scope-out must "carry the notes with their edges," but never says what happens when an edge doesn't survive one-to-one: a split can point one old dependency id at more than one new terminal step (`create.py:_apply_step_split`), and a merge unions two members' external `depends_on` onto a single edge (`create.py:_apply_step_merge`) — so a note could duplicate, collide, or silently drop. `PLAN_FORMAT.md` already carries exactly this kind of mutation table for `intent`; `depends_on_notes` needs the same.
  - Fix: add an acceptance criterion (and expand step 2's/step 6's scope) pinning an explicit fan-out/fan-in policy for `depends_on_notes`, mirroring the existing `intent`-under-mutation table, covering every renumbering site step 2 names.
- MEDIUM `[purity-cache-note-neutrality]`: `plan_tool/fingerprint.py` (not in the plan's "In scope" list) already hashes `step.depends_on` into the purity-cache key as "verdict-affecting frontmatter," while deliberately excluding `title`/`complexity` for not affecting the verdict — and the plan gives no signal which side `depends_on_notes` falls on, despite repeatedly calling it "sibling to depends_on."
  - Fix: add a Testing bullet stating `depends_on_notes` joins the deliberately-excluded set, not the hashed set, with a backward-compat test proving a note-only edit leaves the cached purity key unchanged.
